findings.title: Unattended, unreviewed tofu apply runs as an SA holding project-wide setIamPolicy permissions
findings.explanation: ci.yml's tofu job runs `tofu apply -auto-approve` on every push to main with no human in the loop, using github-actions-terraform. That SA's fuel_terraform role (iam/google_project_iam_custom_role.tf) already carries iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy and resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy project-wide -- the exact pair the repo's own README calls escalation-class and specifically keeps the iam/ module human-apply-only to contain. That containment only covers edits to iam/'s own role definitions. It does nothing for the equivalent outcome via terraform/, which IS auto-applied: a single merged PR adding one additive google_project_iam_member resource there would be picked up and executed unattended. I confirmed via `gh api repos/JamesWoolfenden/garmin-mcp-gt/branches/main/protection` that main has no branch protection (404 Branch not protected), so there is no required-review gate before a push reaches that auto-apply. This isn't something a single-resource or two-resource deterministic rule can see -- it requires correlating the workflow's trigger/approval model, the bound role's permission list in a different Terraform root module, and live GitHub branch-protection state.
findings.remediation: Add required PR reviews + status checks on main (branch protection or a rulest), or move the apply step behind a GitHub Environment with required reviewers, so a merge alone can't trigger an unattended apply by a principal that holds project IAM-policy-write permissions.
findings.decision: Accepted as risk 2026-10-08 -- solo project, single committer. Revisit if a collaborator is ever added or main stops being single-pusher.

findings.title: fuel_terraform_build's storage.objects.* is also bound at project scope, reaching the CMEK sqlite bucket it was never meant for
findings.explanation: fuel_terraform_build bundles storage.objects.{create,get,delete,list} (needed only for tofu's GCS state backend) together with project-scoped-only permissions (secretmanager.versions.access/list, cloudkms.*.list, storage.buckets.list). Because the whole role is bound both at project level (fuel_terraform_build_project, line 108) and at bucket level for the tfstate bucket specifically (fuel_terraform_build_tfstate, line 120), the project-level binding alone already grants github-actions-terraform object read/write/delete on every bucket in the project -- including terraform/sqlite.tf's CMEK-encrypted sqlite bucket, which sqlite.tf's own design (uniform_bucket_level_access, a dedicated storage.objectAdmin binding scoped only to fuel_backend's SA) clearly intends to keep single-accessor. The bucket-scoped binding already covers the one bucket the object permissions are actually for, so the project-level inclusion of those four permissions is pure excess exposure, not a functional need. HLD_GCP_262 (Cloud Storage object-level roles should be granted per bucket, not at project level) exists and covers exactly this pattern for google_project_iam_member -- but its rule only pattern-matches the literal role string against roles/storage.objectViewer|objectCreator|objectAdmin, so it can't see object permissions bundled inside a referenced custom role and never evaluates this resource at all.
findings.remediation: Split fuel_terraform_build further: keep storage.objects.* in a role bound only at bucket scope (fuel_terraform_build_tfstate already does this), and bind the remaining project-scoped-only permissions (secretmanager.versions.*, cloudkms.*.list, storage.buckets.list) via a separate role with no bucket-level duplicate.
findings.decision: Fixed and applied live 2026-10-08. fuel_terraform_build trimmed to storage.objects.* only, bound exclusively at bucket scope. The other 5 permissions moved to a new fuel_terraform_build_metadata role, bound only at project level. Net permission set on the SA unchanged -- verified identical before/after via diff. HLD_GCP_555 no longer fires (holden scan iam: 0 failed / 311 passed).

findings.title: Cloud Scheduler's internal-secret header goes stale on rotation while Cloud Run's copy updates live
findings.explanation: scheduler.tf's http_target.headers["X-Internal-Secret"] is set from var.internal_secret, but `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [http_target[0].headers] }` meant Terraform never re-applied that header after the first apply, while google_cloud_run_v2_service.fuel_backend.tf's secret_key_ref (version = "latest") always tracks the current Secret Manager value -- an asymmetry that would silently break the daily nudge job's auth on any secret rotation.
findings.remediation: Removed the `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [http_target[0].headers] }` block from google_cloud_scheduler_job.nudge in terraform/scheduler.tf (2026-10-08). The original commit (d919668) that added it gave no reason; user confirmed no known reason to keep it.

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_262 blocks roles/storage.objectViewer|objectCreator|objectAdmin from being granted via google_project_iam_member/_binding, but only matches those three literal predefined-role strings on the `role` attribute. A custom role (google_project_iam_custom_role) that bundles storage.objects.* permissions and gets bound the same way via its `.id` reference is invisible to that check -- confirmed against this repo's iam/google_project_iam_custom_role.tf, where fuel_terraform_build_project does exactly this. The existing `linked_resource` + `none_match` primitives (already in the live schema) are sufficient to express it with no new DSL primitive needed. Implemented as HLD_GCP_555 and pushed directly to JamesWoolfenden/holden main (2026-10-08) -- policy, fixture, and test all included.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_555
name: Custom roles granting Cloud Storage object permissions must not be bound at project level
cloud: gcp
principle: identity-and-access
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  A custom role containing storage.objects.* permissions, bound via
  google_project_iam_member/_binding, grants that access to every bucket in
  the project -- including buckets created later -- not just the one the
  workload actually needs. HLD_GCP_262 catches this for the three predefined
  storage object roles (objectViewer/objectCreator/objectAdmin) but can't see
  inside a referenced custom role's permission list, so the same over-exposure
  via a custom role goes undetected.
message: |
  This project-level IAM member binds a custom role that grants
  storage.objects.* permissions project-wide. Scope it to the specific
  bucket(s) needed with a google_storage_bucket_iam_member instead.
remediation: |
  Replace (or supplement) the project-level binding with a bucket-scoped one:

  resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "state" {
    bucket = google_storage_bucket.tfstate.name
    role   = google_project_iam_custom_role.custom.id
    member = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.ci.email}"
  }
resources:
  google_project_iam_member:
    linked_resource:
      attr: role
      type: google_project_iam_custom_role
      where:
        path: permissions
        none_match: "^storage\\.objects\\."
  google_project_iam_binding:
    linked_resource:
      attr: role
      type: google_project_iam_custom_role
      where:
        path: permissions
        none_match: "^storage\\.objects\\."
